headline: SILVER CRATERS TO 14-MONTH LOW AT $41 — Spot Hits Worst Level Since September 2025 as Dollar Surge Erases Year's Gains
snippet: Silver opened November 20 at its lowest point in 14 months — around $41/oz — after a 30-day plunge of roughly 28% driven by a surging US dollar and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes. Net long positioning in silver fell to its lowest since February 2024, pointing to continued near-term pressure even as UBS maintains a longer-term target of $60/oz by mid-2027. The metal's break below long-term support around $50 and the gold/silver ratio at its highest since late 2025 have rattled junior silver miners across the TSX-V and ASX.

headline: COPPER ENTERS BEAR MARKET, ERASING ALL 2026 GAINS — LME Hits $12,235/t in Worst Week of Year; NYC Already 20% Below September Peak
snippet: Copper officially entered bear market territory on November 20, with LME three-month copper falling 2.3% to $12,235/t — 18% below its September peak — while New York copper crossed the 20% bear-market threshold, erasing all of 2026's gains. Rising LME warehouse inventories of 320,000 tonnes, a stronger US dollar, and doubts about AI-related infrastructure spending are cited as the primary drivers, while UBS argues the move is a positioning and sentiment reset rather than a structural demand collapse. The selloff has hammered copper-focused juniors and majors alike, with BHP touching a seven-month low.

headline: BHP SHARES CRATER 13% TO 7-MONTH LOW IN ONE WEEK — Copper Rout Hammers World's Largest Miner; Analysts Ask: Time to Buy?
snippet: BHP Group (ASX: BHP) shed 13% over five trading days ending November 20, hitting a seven-month low as the copper bear market more than offset the company's strong FY26 underlying profit of US$13.2 billion — the year copper overtook iron ore as BHP's largest earnings contributor. Analyst consensus sits at a price target of A$77.25, well above current levels, suggesting the market may be pricing in a prolonged commodity downturn. For investors in copper-focused juniors, BHP's directional move is a leading indicator of sector sentiment heading into the weekend.

headline: LIT LITHIUM MINERS FUND FALLS TO 12-MONTH LOW AT $51.98 — Seventh Straight Down Session Hits Albemarle, SQM as Surplus Fears Deepen
snippet: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) fell 4.33% on November 20 to US$51.98, a 12-month low, completing seven consecutive down sessions as Albemarle, SQM, and other major producers faced renewed pressure from fears of a lithium surplus stretching into 2027. The decline mirrors the spot lithium carbonate market, where Citi this month cut its price forecast by 40% on weaker-than-expected EV demand growth. Guangzhou Futures Exchange is set to launch new lithium hydroxide futures on November 26, adding a fresh price discovery mechanism that could bring short-term volatility but longer-term transparency.

headline: RARE EARTH SELLOFF EXTENDS — Critical Metals -8%, USA Rare Earth -5% as Trump-Xi Rally Fades; Sector Still Down 42% YTD
snippet: Rare earth stocks gave back their November 19 White House-inspired bounce on November 20, with Critical Metals tumbling 8%, USA Rare Earth (USAR) falling 5% to around $6.51, and MP Materials dropping 3%, extending a week of whipsaw trading around US-China diplomatic signals. Despite the White House pledge to close the gap with China, USA Rare Earth remains down approximately 42% year-to-date and faces feedstock shortage headwinds at its Less Common Metals unit flagged in a recent William Blair downgrade. China's export licensing rules on seven medium and heavy rare earths — in force since April 2025 — remain active through at least January 2027.

headline: ATOMIC EAGLE FINDS NEW URANIUM ZONES AT MUNTANGA, ZAMBIA — Two of Eight Targets Confirm Mineralization; Drilling Focus Narrowed
snippet: Atomic Eagle reported two new mineralized zones at its Muntanga uranium project in Zambia on November 20, narrowing the drill focus after six of eight Muntanga North targets returned no significant uranium values. The discovery expands the drill-ready pipeline at a project showing consistent shallow ISR-style mineralization in Zambia's Luangwa Basin, one of Africa's most active emerging uranium exploration addresses. With Aura Energy's Tiris project advancing in Mauritania and Atomic Eagle progressing in Zambia, junior uranium exploration in Africa is building momentum ahead of a potential spot price recovery.

headline: NEW MEXICO AG WINS INTERVENTION IN NUFUELS CROWNPOINT URANIUM LICENSE RENEWAL — NRC Grants State Standing; Formal Hearing Now Required
snippet: The New Mexico Attorney General's office was granted intervenor status by the NRC in the license renewal for NuFuels Inc.'s Crownpoint Uranium Project — a four-area ISR operation covering Church Rock Sections 8 and 17, Unit 1, and Crownpoint in McKinley County — triggering a formal adjudicatory hearing before any renewal can proceed. The state cited proximity of the Church Rock areas to the White Cliffs domestic water supply system serving area communities. The case is one of the highest-profile state-level challenges to uranium mining permitting in the US in the current ISR licence renewal cycle and could set a precedent for future state interventions.

headline: VIRIDIAN METALS CONTINUES BROAD NEAR-SURFACE MINERALIZATION AT KRAKEN MAIN — 16 Holes Assaying; Target 41-61Mt at 0.35-0.52% CuEq
snippet: Viridian Metals (CSE: VRDN) reported continued broad near-surface copper-equivalent mineralization at Kraken Main in Newfoundland and Labrador, with assays pending from 16 additional drill holes that could extend the project's initial exploration target of 41-61 million tonnes at 0.35-0.52% CuEq. September 2026 assay batches returned 50.15m @ 0.68% CuEq from 1m, establishing consistent shallow mineralization across a 3-kilometre sulphide corridor, while the company's recently closed $5.77 million private placement fully funds its 2027 drilling program. The scale and near-surface nature of Kraken Main make it one of the more compelling copper-equivalent development-stage stories in Atlantic Canada.

headline: LITHIUM AFRICA FINDS NEW PEGMATITE SYSTEM AT JACKAL WATER — 11km From Norrabees; First Holes Return Up to 2.21% Li₂O
snippet: Lithium Africa (TSX-V: LAF) disclosed a new lithium pegmatite system at Jackal Water, 11 km from the Norrabees cluster at its flagship Springbok Project in South Africa's Northern Cape, with initial drill holes returning up to 2.21% Li₂O over 1.0 metre. The discovery builds the company's target inventory at Springbok, a 1,675 km² property where it targets first spodumene concentrate in H2 2027 pending processing plant permitting. The Jackal Water system adds district-scale credibility to what has been a largely single-cluster story, potentially de-risking the broader project for investors.

headline: SCORPION MINERALS SIGNS DEAL FOR PAYNES FIND GOLD PROJECT, WESTERN AUSTRALIA — 289km² Ties Into Nearby Kirkalocka Gold Ground
snippet: Scorpion Minerals (ASX: SCN) signed a binding term sheet on November 19 to acquire 100% of the Paynes Find Gold Project — a 289 km² ground position in WA's Paynes Find district — with the largest cash payments structured as contingent milestones tied to resource outcomes. The acquisition is designed to complement Scorpion's nearby Kirkalocka Gold Project, potentially building a combined district-scale land package in one of Western Australia's productive but under-drilled greenstone gold corridors. The deal is typical of the junior consolidation of WA gold ground that often accelerates when the gold price retreats.

headline: BLUE MOON METALS CLOSES TURNER COPPER-GOLD ACQUISITION IN OREGON — US$4.7M Cash + 4.78M Shares to Gold Coast Mining
snippet: Blue Moon Metals (TSX-V: MOON) closed the acquisition of the Turner copper-gold deposit in Oregon, paying US$4.7 million in cash and issuing approximately 4.78 million common shares to vendor Gold Coast Mining, adding a scalable near-surface copper-gold asset in a permitting-friendly US state. The deal closes into a sharp copper bear market, which may weigh on near-term re-rating, but positions the company with US-domiciled copper-gold optionality at a time when Washington is actively encouraging domestic copper production. Turner joins a growing list of Oregon copper-gold projects attracting junior capital from Canadian-listed vehicles.

headline: 'AI ANXIETY IS TURNING INTO A GROWTH SCARE' — UBS Sees Copper Rout as Sentiment Reset, Not Structural Reversal
source_name: The Dark Side of the Boom
snippet: UBS commodity analysts argue that the worst week of 2026 for copper is not simply a China demand story but reflects doubts about AI-driven data centre copper demand morphing into a broader growth scare, contributing to a positioning unwind now visible in LME warehouse builds and New York's bear-market crossing. The bank cuts near-term copper price forecasts while maintaining its long-run structural deficit view — framing any demand confirmation as a sharp re-entry signal for copper stocks. For junior copper investors, the distinction between a sentiment reset and a structural collapse matters enormously for position sizing through this correction.

headline: 'THE URANIUM PRICE PARADOX' — Spot at $91 While Miners Bleed: 5 Stocks Facing Very Different Tests Heading Into 2027
snippet: An Investing.com analysis examines the uranium sector's widening disconnect: spot at $91/lb and Cameco's long-term indicator above $98/lb, yet the Sprott Uranium Miners ETF has fallen roughly 56% from its January 2026 high of $84.95. The piece profiles five uranium investments facing very different pressures in 2027, including Cameco's narrowed 2026 production guidance (19.5-20.5Mlbs, affected by Key Lake mill maintenance) and Uranium Energy's White Mesa restart targeted for December. The spot-to-equity divergence rarely persists indefinitely — either contracts reprice down or equity eventually catches up to contract reality.
